title: The Unofficial Guide to Apple’s Private Cloud Compute - Jmo, CONFSEC
talk_summary: A security talk explaining Apple's Private Cloud Compute architecture (stateless compute, remote attestation, transparency logs, oblivious HTTP, blind signatures) and how similar primitives are available off-Apple via TPMs, confidential VMs, and Sigstore/Sigsum. It is about privacy-preserving remote inference infrastructure, not about agent orchestration, review quality, or model routing.

takeaways.what_they_do: Maintain an append-only, Merkle-tree log of every signed software release/component so anyone can verify offline that what a server attests to running matches a public record; an attestation not on the log implies compromise.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you see an attestation that's not on the log you know the whole system's been compromised

takeaways.what_they_do: Client asks server what it is running, gets signed claims plus a public key, and only encrypts data to that key if claims match a trusted version; server can only decrypt while still matching those claims.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I can only decrypt it as long as it's still running the exact thing I said I trusted

takeaways.technique: Enforceable guarantees over policy (no SSH, no disk)
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of relying on policy ('don't SSH', 'don't log'), they remove the capability: no sshd, no disk, so statelessness is structural rather than promised.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Not I shouldn't SSH to the instance, but I can SSH to the instances. No, there's no SSH on the instance.

takeaways.technique: Oblivious HTTP / anonymizing proxy for outbound model calls
takeaways.what_they_do: Route requests through a third-party relay so the inference provider sees the relay's IP, not the user's, decoupling identity from request.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all of the request that goes to Apple's private cloud compute first goes through Cloudflare
